items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: how about a guy like Eddie Diehl, the guitar player? Great player. I don’t think he could read.

ctx.x: Here’s a question about, over the years I’m sure you’ve played with people in different situations who were not readers, who were self-taught, often times guitar players. I wonder if you almost surprisingly learned anything from those self-taught musicians?

Well the first one I learned from was Erroll Garner on his records. He was self-taught. He couldn’t read music. And years later Woody Herman made a record, a duet record with him and we were playing at Basin Street and they were promoting that record and they invited Erroll to come and play with the band, you know it was like a three-tune medley that modulated. And he sat in and played. He couldn’t read the chart at all, but he just played it by ear you know. So as far as people who couldn’t read, how about a guy…

I concur. And I’ve learned from some of the guitar players especially that their ears are so tuned in because they learned that way, and they sometimes think of things compositionally that schooled musicians may not because it doesn’t follow certain chord
